# Influint channel intelligence

An evidence base about what actually moves YouTube performance, built from measured
retention curves rather than from advice. 237 channels are tracked and
19 carry per-video retention analysis. Every claim carries how well it has
held up, on how many independent channels, and what it does not establish.

READ THIS FIRST. Most of this knowledge base has never been quantified. That is the
honest state of it, not a gap being papered over: the probes reach retention curves,
runtime, views, titles, click-through where a Studio pull exists, and detected video
segments. Claims about thumbnails and audience psychology sit outside that reach and
are on the record because a practitioner asserted them. Never present a claim as
established without checking its standing and its limits.

## Connect over MCP (recommended)

One file, no dependencies, Node 18 or newer.

1. Download: https://majieddd.github.io/influint-channels-public/yt-intelligence-mcp.mjs
2. Ask your contact at Influint for an API key. It is read-only.
3. Add to your MCP client config:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "yt-intelligence": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["/absolute/path/to/yt-intelligence-mcp.mjs"],
      "env": {
        "YT_INTELLIGENCE_URL": "<ask Influint for the API host>",
        "YT_INTELLIGENCE_KEY": "<your key>"
      }
    }
  }
}

For Claude Code: claude mcp add yt-intelligence --env YT_INTELLIGENCE_URL=<ask Influint for the API host> --env YT_INTELLIGENCE_KEY=<your key> -- node /absolute/path/to/yt-intelligence-mcp.mjs

## Connect over HTTP

NOTE: this build has no API host configured, so the address below is a
placeholder. Ask your contact at Influint for the host as well as the key.

Every endpoint is GET, returns JSON, and needs a bearer token:

  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <your key>" "<ask Influint for the API host>/state"

- GET /api/intelligence/state
  tool name: intelligence_state
  params: none
  How much of the knowledge base is measured, how many claims share one test, and what is waiting on a human. Call it first.
- GET /api/intelligence/claims
  tool name: intelligence_claims
  params: niche, category, standing, measuredOnly, limit
  The claims that apply to a channel, routed by niche, WITH the prohibitions: things our own data refuted. Says what it omitted.
- GET /api/intelligence/claim?id=<id>
  tool name: intelligence_claim_evidence
  params: id (required)
  One claim's full record: the probe, every per-channel reading, the niche breakdown, and an explicit list of what it does NOT establish.
- GET /api/intelligence/actions?channelId=<UC...>
  tool name: channel_action_list
  params: channelId (required)
  The prioritised moves for one channel, ordered by viewers recoverable, each with the confidence behind it.
- GET /api/intelligence/channels
  tool name: list_channels
  params: none
  Every channel in the knowledge base, with niche, scale band and analysis depth.
- GET /api/intelligence/workflows
  tool name: list_workflows
  params: none
  The ways this system is operated, each with what it looks at and the ONLY modes it may apply a claim in. Read this first.
- GET /api/intelligence/workflow?id=<id>
  tool name: workflow_intelligence
  params: id (required), niche, limit
  The claims one workflow may apply, bucketed by mode: rules, priors (with evidence), hypotheses, prohibitions, do-not-repeat. A theory never arrives as a rule.

A 503 means the API is switched off on that deployment, not that your key is wrong.
A 401 means the key is missing or wrong. Both responses say which.

## How to read an answer

- standing: Where a claim sits on the evidence ladder. theory = nobody has measured it. candidate-law = measured once with a real effect. law = reproduced across channels AND signed by a person. warning = a known failure mode. Standing moves DOWN as well as up.
- evidence.units / unitNoun: How many INDEPENDENT things the reading rests on, and what kind of thing. Three readings from one crawl are not three channels, so the noun is never assumed.
- evidence.causalRung: What kind of claim the evidence can support: correlation, consistent, dose-response, temporal, intervention. Earned by the DESIGN of the test, never read off the effect size. A hundred consistent correlations are still a correlation.
- evidence.grade: How much the evidence supports ACTING: untested, weak, moderate, strong. Separate axis from causalRung, deliberately.
- limits: What this claim does NOT establish, generated from its own record. Read it before repeating the claim as fact.
- prohibitions: Claims our data refuted. These travel with every answer because they are the most valuable thing here and the easiest to leave behind.

## What it will not do

It is read-only, and that is the safety boundary rather than a limitation. It cannot
start an analysis, publish anything, or move a claim's standing. Standing moves on a
measurement or on a human signature; an endpoint that let a caller edit it would make
both meaningless.
